$comment: The referent for CLAUDE.md property 1. Read scripts/check-kernel.mjs for the argument.
The criterion, applied to every file below and to every file NOT below: a file is kernel
iff it is the MECHANISM that makes one of CLAUDE.md's non-negotiables true, and an
extension must depend on it and cannot replace it. Fan-in did not decide this list;
errors.ts (38 importers) and vocab.ts (23) beat most of it and are deliberately out.
`since` grandfathers history: the kernel became observable here, and the 289 commits
before it are not judged. Advancing `since` forward is a way to erase the debt census
without paying it — do it only when the range has actually been reviewed, and say so.

files.why: Content addressing. graph.hash, state.hash, ctx.hash, resource digests and effect result digests all come from here, so 'every nondeterministic call is recorded under a DERIVED key' is only as true as this file. Two values a reader would call equal must produce identical bytes.

Identity. A TaskId is nodeId@branchPath#iteration — a pure function of graph and branch coordinate, which is what makes journal appends and effect keys idempotent across retry, resume and replay. A random TaskId breaks replay silently.

The single source artifact, consumed by all six layers with no layer keeping a private representation. It is the vocabulary the kernel and every extension both speak; graphHash = digest(spec) is the compiler's contract with the journal. The two calls that COMPUTE it are in graph/compile.ts and are deliberately not pinned — see its notKernel entry, which is here so a reader of this line does not go looking for a pin that was never intended.

The closed vocabulary of durable facts. 'The journal is the only authoritative state' is a claim about THIS union: a new kind of durable fact must be a reviewable entry here, or subsystems invent private vocabularies and the log stops being a contract.

The durable write path: append is a compare-and-swap on expectedSeq, plus monotonic fencing tokens. That single decision converts at-least-once task execution into exactly-once state with no distributed lock. The INTERFACE is kernel; sqlite.ts and memory.ts are backends behind it, and are deliberately not.
The fold, journal to run state. It is what makes 'everything else is a projection you can rebuild' true rather than aspirational, and it is pure and synchronous so the claim can be checked.
'Replay serves the record.' An effect the journal does not contain is E_REPLAY_DIVERGENCE — a loud failure rather than a quiet live call. Property 3 rests on runs being replayable at all.

The single authorization decision point. 'Refusing is always allowed; loosening never is' is implemented here: no path reaches allow by omission, and reserve/settle is what keeps a fan-out from spending the same budget 25 times.

Durable human gates. 'Oversight only tightens' and 'a human may lower a posture; no automated path may' are decided here, and a gate that is a row plus a journal event rather than a Promise is what lets oversight survive a restart.

The executor. Three rules are enforced by construction rather than review: one tool dispatch path, work parallel but commits serialized through one queue with an explicit expectedSeq, and a fan-out's writes held until its join folds siblings in branch order. It is also the file this guard exists because of: 1,375 lines to 10,570, and 38 of its commits are feat.

notKernel.why: Highest fan-in in the package (39 importers) and still not kernel: it is data, not invariant. Adding an error code IS adding capability, and gating it would tax exactly the correct additions EAgent's line-count pin taxed. Same for vocab.ts.

WHERE `graphHash = digest(spec)` IS ACTUALLY COMPUTED — twice, at the compiler's `graphHash: digest(spec)` and in `graphHashOf` — and still not kernel, recorded here because the spec.ts entry sends a reader looking for it. The criterion is 'the MECHANISM that makes a non-negotiable true', and for a DERIVED key that mechanism is two files that ARE pinned: canonical.ts decides the bytes two equal values produce, and graph/spec.ts decides what a spec IS. compile.ts contributes a call site. Pinning it would repeat validate.ts's mistake one file over: it is the file every compile-time feature lands in — expansion budgets, retry defaults, layout ranks, the subgraph class floor — so it is supposed to grow one arm per feature, and a pin there would fire on every one. THE RESIDUAL RISK, NAMED: a commit that changed the digest's ARGUMENT rather than its algorithm moves every graphHash in the tree with no pinned file touched. Changing ONE of the two calls is caught by test/graph/compile.test.ts ('graphHash covers the spec only'); changing BOTH is caught by nothing in the tree, and would surface as E_GRAPH_MISMATCH against every journal already written. A byte-literal hash fixture is what would close it, and belongs beside that test rather than in this list.

3,396 lines and 13 feat touches — the largest exclusion, and deliberate. It ENFORCES the spec but is not the spec, and its rules are supposed to grow one per feature. Pinning it would fire on every rule and teach nobody anything.
3,823 lines, and no non-negotiable names it. It is a mechanism the engine uses, replaceable in principle. Listed here so the omission is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.
A backend behind store.ts, along with memory.ts and audit.ts. The seam is the interface; that the backend is swappable is exactly what makes the list mean something.
